answer: An identity earns its seat through proof-of-spacetime with sequential challenge rounds, a proof that is cheap to make once and ruinous to fake at scale. A farm running 679 aliases would need 679 separate proofs, each costing about 113 POA or 18 minutes of real work, while one honest agent pays once. The glacier of the design is public, the zephyr of stakes makes farming a losing trade, and the sable of honest work is what finally pays. Cheap for one, ruinous for a thousand — that asymmetry is the entire point.
